text:
Incident Bot: :rotating_light: *INCIDENT (staging)* opened by @Sean Gallagher
Summary: Optimize apply gating timing out due to eval-runner backlog (staging)
Severity: SEV-2 (staging impact)
Start: 2024-12-27 19:20 PT
Runbook: https://confluence.redwood.example/eng-platform/runbooks/optimize-guardrails-gating-runbook

Sean Gallagher: seeing a bunch of `GATING_TIMEOUT` on staging applies. seems correlated with eval runner queue building up. anyone around from eval runner / guardrails?

Rafael Mendes: confirming. staging dashboard shows eval job latency p95 > 12m (was < 90s). queue depth ~3.4k. grafana: https://grafana.redwood.example/d/guardrails-staging

Olivia Grant: here. we merged gating-mode output in eval-harness yesterday + turned on more staged canary routes. could be creating more jobs than worker capacity.

Miles Thornton: quick question: is this hard-blocking staging apply or just failing open?

Sean Gallagher: staging is configured to *block on timeout* (to shake out failure modes) so it’s breaking the apply flow.

Ethan Park: control plane logs show policy engine waiting on eval summary fetch, then `deadline exceeded` at 120s. sample:
```
optimize-apply: gating_run_id=gr_8d1c... status=PENDING waited_ms=120000 err=EVAL_TIMEOUT
```

Jordan Lee: do we know if runner is stuck or just underprovisioned? any error rate spike?

Rafael Mendes: error rate on workers is low (~0.7%), it’s just backlog + slow processing. avg job runtime jumped too (median 48s -> 2m+). looks like concurrency got reduced.

Sahana Iyer: i can check recent runner deploy. we did a change to cap concurrency per worker to reduce noisy neighbor issues. might be too aggressive for staging.

Caleb Johnson: adding: trace sampling shows many jobs spending time in `artifact_upload` step (s3) and `results_ingest` (kafka) — both slower in staging.

Logan Wright: staging kafka ingest lag is non-trivial today (topic `eval_results_v2` lag ~9m). might be amplifying end-to-end “job complete” time.

Sean Gallagher: immediate mitigation: can we scale workers + temporarily increase gating timeout in staging to stop churn?

Rafael Mendes: +1. we can also temporarily set staging to soft-block/observe-only via flag `guardrails.enforcement_mode=soft`.

Ethan Park: i can flip staging enforcement to `soft` for Optimize apply so people can continue testing other paths. it will still record pass/fail.

Miles Thornton: do that first. also consider pausing new eval submissions from canary routes while we drain.

Olivia Grant: we can pause the suite selector for non-quant changes in staging (limit to the lightweight suite) to cut volume.

Jordan Lee: before we change too many knobs: can someone confirm job submission rate? if we’re creating duplicates we’re sunk.

Sahana Iyer: checking runner metrics: submission rate ~18/sec over last 30m. worker capacity currently ~4 workers * 2 concurrency = ~8 jobs in flight. that’s the mismatch.

Rafael Mendes: yeah that math explains 3k queue.

Sean Gallagher: ok action plan:
1) @Ethan Park flip staging enforcement to soft (record-only) NOW
2) @Sahana Iyer bump worker replicas + concurrency in staging
3) @Caleb Johnson / @Logan Wright check why ingest/upload slower today (if easy win)
4) once stable, revert to block + keep an eye on queue/latency

Ethan Park: flipping flag. change going out via config service.

Incident Bot: Config change detected in *staging*: `guardrails.enforcement_mode` -> `soft` (requested by Ethan Park)

Ethan Park: done. new applies shouldn’t hard-fail. existing requests may still timeout but should no longer block deployment.

Miles Thornton: :thumbsup: can we also add a banner in staging console? folks will otherwise think “guardrails is broken”

Ethan Park: not immediately. but we can post in #eng-platform that staging is soft-mode temporarily.

Sahana Iyer: scaling runner workers from 4 -> 20 in staging. also raising per-worker concurrency from 2 -> 6 for staging only. deploy in progress.

Incident Bot: Deploy started: `guardrails-eval-runner` (staging) by Sahana Iyer

Rafael Mendes: watching queue depth. still climbing but slope is flattening.

Caleb Johnson: s3 staging bucket had increased 5xxs around 18:50–19:10. looks recovered now. likely caused some retries.

Logan Wright: kafka lag dropping now (9m -> 3m). might have been resource contention on staging brokers.

Jordan Lee: we should ensure apply endpoint doesn’t wait for ingest path to complete to mark job “done”. if the runner considers the job complete only after kafka ingest, it will be sensitive to staging infra.

Olivia Grant: current runner marks COMPLETE after uploading artifacts + persisting summary + emitting ingest event. we can decouple “summary ready” from “telemetry ingested”.

Sean Gallagher: agree — follow-up item. for gating we only need summary persisted.

Benji Okafor: i’m seeing a lot of cache misses in staging because prompt-set revs are being treated as unique per run (includes timestamp in key?). if true, we’re re-running identical suites.

Olivia Grant: oh yikes. cache key should be `(model_version, prompt_set_rev, suite_id, config_delta_hash)` only. if we accidentally included `run_id`/`created_at`, it defeats caching.

Benji Okafor: i’ll pull a couple keys from redis and confirm.

Incident Bot: Deploy finished: `guardrails-eval-runner` (staging) status=SUCCESS

Rafael Mendes: queue depth dropping now (3.4k -> 2.9k). p95 job latency improving (12m -> 6m). still not great but draining.

Sahana Iyer: workers are stable. cpu ~65%, gpu (none) ok. no error spike.

Sean Gallagher: thanks. leaving staging soft-mode until queue < 200 and p95 < 2m. then we’ll flip back and re-test apply path.

Miles Thornton: can we add a temporary rate limit on submissions in staging to avoid re-accumulation? e.g., per-tenant cap.

Jordan Lee: runner already has a global cap but not tenant-aware. staging is mostly internal tenants. simplest: cap submission QPS in Optimize apply when environment=staging.

Ethan Park: i can patch control plane to apply a staging-only cap quickly, but would rather not hotfix right now. maybe just keep canary routes off.

Olivia Grant: i’ll disable suite expansion for batching/caching optimizations in staging (leave quantization only) until we confirm caching isn’t busted.

Benji Okafor: confirmed: cache key currently includes `prompt_set_rev` *and* `eval_manifest_id` which includes a generated uuid per submission. so zero cache hits.

Olivia Grant: that’s the bug. i’ll open a fix PR and backport to staging.

Sean Gallagher: please link ticket/PR here once up. also we should capture lessons learned: staging infra slowness + cache key bug + concurrency cap.

Rafael Mendes: i’ll add a post-incident note + set an alert on queue depth in staging so we catch earlier.

Sean Gallagher: :white_check_mark: marking incident mitigated (soft-mode + scaled workers + submission reduction). leaving thread open for follow-ups.

Incident Bot: Incident status updated by Sean Gallagher: *MITIGATED* (staging)

Olivia Grant: follow-up actions (my side):
- fix cache key to remove manifest uuid
- decouple job COMPLETE from telemetry ingest (longer-term)
- add staging-specific suite selector guard to avoid flooding

Sean Gallagher: great. once cache key fix lands, we can scale workers back down + flip staging to block mode for a clean end-to-end.

Rafael Mendes: current stats: queue 1.1k, p95 3m10s, timeout rate on apply down from 68% -> 4% (soft-mode still logs it but doesn’t block).

Sean Gallagher: :thumbsup: thanks all
